name: Mahanagar Gas Ltd
title: Mahanagar Gas Ltd - 539957 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

read.thesis: City gas distributor under LNG supply curtailment: I&C supply cut to ~80%, March volumes lost ~20-22% in industrial, but FY26 volume grew 8.25% and management targets 10%+ FY27 growth with ~INR1,200 crore capex.

summary.headline: MGL Q4 FY26 net profit fell to INR132 crore from INR202 crore QoQ as West Asia LNG disruption curtailed industrial supply to about 80%.
summary.overview: Q4 FY26 average sales volume rose 6.15% YoY to 4.672 mmscmd, with CNG at 3.349 mmscmd and DPNG at 0.605 mmscmd. Industrial and commercial supply was curtailed to about 80% from mid-March after the West Asia LNG disruption, and gas cost rose as the pooled gas mechanism replaced part of Henry Hub supply. FY26 EBITDA fell to INR1,451 crore from INR1,570 crore and PAT to INR847 crore from INR1,041 crore. Management declined to give firm FY27 margin guidance, saying it would prioritise volume growth and pass through costs only where alternate-fuel pricing allows.

segments.name: CNG
segments.commentary: Q4 FY26 volume 3.349 mmscmd, up 7.12% YoY from 3.125 mmscmd. Fleet reached 12,84,828 vehicles, with 1,18,590 added in FY26.

segments.name: Domestic PNG
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 0.605 mmscmd, up 2.24% YoY. Sourced 100% from APM gas. Management said domestic volume grew about 6.6% YoY, disputing a question on a decline.

segments.name: Industrial and commercial
segments.commentary: Q4 volume 0.719 mmscmd, up 4.87% YoY. Industrial supply was curtailed to about 80%, with industrial volume down about 20-22% in March versus February. FY26 I&C volume grew 15.04% per management.

guidance_outlook: Management expects FY27 volume growth above the 8.25% achieved in FY26 and possibly double digit if connection pace holds; it cited easier road-digging permissions and a 24 March notification cutting road reinstatement charges by more than half.
Management would like to maintain EBITDA above INR8 per SCM for FY27 but declined to give a firm margin number, citing uncertainty over RLNG supply.
FY27 capex is expected at around INR1,200 crore, possibly somewhat higher subject to labour and material availability.
A CNG price increase of INR1/kg took effect on 22 April 2026. Management said CNG is not fully passed through and further hikes depend on sustained high costs and alternate-fuel prices.
Management said monsoon in June-July may slow pipeline laying on public roads.
capex_capacity: Q4 FY26: 1,43,997 domestic households connected; FY26: 3,42,157 connected, cumulative about 3.21 million.
FY26 network additions: 499 km of steel and PE pipeline, total over 8,320 km; Q4 added 138.48 km.
CNG stations: 28 added in Q4 and 52 in FY26, taking the total to 518 as on 31 March 2026.
Industrial and commercial customers: 334 added in Q4 and 872 in FY26, taking the total to 5,924.
Management expects to add 4-5 lakh DPNG customers, against about 2 million currently burning DPNG.
demand_pricing: Supply mix in March: APM about 1.6 mmscmd; NWG plus pooled gas about 0.73-0.75 mmscmd; HPHT about 0.9 mmscmd (term plus exchange); Henry Hub cut to about 50% of the 1.5 mmscmd contracted quantity.
Q4 averages: APM more than 1.73 mmscmd; HPHT about 0.7 mmscmd; NWG a little over 0.4 mmscmd; Henry Hub about 0.78 mmscmd.
Pooled gas applied from about 12 March; about two-thirds of March was affected. Spot LNG priced at about $11.5-13/mmbtu, occasionally $14; management said May pooled gas was around $11-11.5.
DPNG price rise of INR1 on 22 April 2026 was said to cover the APM cost increase from the Kirit Parikh committee circular (about $0.25) and the exchange rate effect.
I&C realisations improved because alternate-fuel-linked pricing follows Brent, which is now at $90-100 against $60-70 earlier. Management noted Henry Hub has stabilised below $3.

qa_highlights.question: How much did March volumes fall, and what is the supply outlook for April and May?
qa_highlights.answer: Industrial supply (excluding commercial) fell by about 1.25-1.3 lakh scmd, roughly 20-22%, from a February average of about 5.75 lakh scmd. April was similar and May showed some improvement, and management did not guide on the pool mix.

qa_highlights.question: Is the gas cost increase covered by price hikes?
qa_highlights.answer: DPNG's INR1 hike covers the APM increase. CNG has not been fully passed through, and management expects to absorb short-term volatility unless costs stay high.

qa_highlights.question: What is the outlook for FY27 volume and margin?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said FY27 volume growth could exceed 8% and could reach double digits if connections accelerate. It gave no firm margin number, but aims to stay above INR8 per SCM EBITDA, and said volume gets priority over margin.

qa_highlights.question: Why sign Brent-linked contracts when Henry Hub is cheaper, and why was HH cut in March?
qa_highlights.answer: Some Brent-linked contracts were signed earlier. HH was cut by force majeure and pooling, and management had no visibility on the pooling price or its end date.

qa_highlights.question: What is the CNG and DPNG growth outlook, and how does capex change?
qa_highlights.answer: Piped gas is expected to drive growth, with CNG at normal rates. Capex is guided at about INR1,200 crore, with some reorientation toward pipelines and lower RI costs.

risks_watch: Continued curtailment of industrial supply to about 80% and pooled gas share, which depends on GAIL allocations and West Asia developments.
CNG margin squeeze if the INR1 hike is not followed by further pass-through; the next-quarter EBITDA per SCM is at risk.
Monsoon slowdown in pipeline laying from June-July and labour and material constraints on connections.
Henry Hub volumes (1.5 mmscmd contracted) and the force majeure exposure; HPHT availability expected in Q2.
Q1 FY27 margins likely below Q4, per the analyst's read, with the INR8 per SCM FY27 target uncertain.
summary.management_tone: Cautious on near-term margins and supply, with management repeatedly declining to quantify FY27 margins or pool mix. Confident on long-term volume growth from PNG conversions and easier permissions.
key_quotes: Our LNG supplies are disrupted due to West Asia crisis and hence supply to industrial and commercial customers is curtailed to approximately 80% as per tariff time to time, impacting the volumes adversely.
Our focus on increasing infrastructure and volumes will be at a slightly higher priority than maintaining margins.
Certainly, it will be whatever we have been giving, INR1,200 crores range.

growth.why: Management says FY27 volume growth could be about 10% (above FY26's 8.25%) if customer connections accelerate, backed by 3.42 lakh households connected and 52 new CNG stations in FY26, with FY27 capex around INR1,200 crore; but no firm margin guidance (only an aspiration to keep EBITDA above INR8/SCM) and Q4 I&C volume was curtailed to about 80% by RLNG disruption.
